findings.claim: Expo package scripts still receive HOST=127.0.0.1 in LAN mode: cli.ts computes isExpo from path.basename(commandArgs[0]) ('bun'), so the LAN carve-out never fires, while cli-utils correctly omits --host through the same script
findings.evidence: probe against the built helpers at 1aba57e: injectPackageScriptFrameworkFlags(['bun','run','expo'],4321) with PORTLESS_LAN=1 returns ['bun','run','expo','--port','4321'] (--host correctly omitted); cli.ts:1391-1394 read directly, hostBind = '127.0.0.1' for the same command
findings.layer: consumer split of a discovery rule

findings.claim: A trailing shell comment in a package script silently discards every injected flag: injection proceeds, the shell drops the tail, the framework keeps its default port and the route 502s
findings.evidence: script "dev": "printf 'ARGS:[%s]\n' \"$*\" # start the dev server"; `bun run dev --port 4321 --strictPort` echoed the composed line and printed ARGS:[] — zero arguments delivered, exit 0, no error. isCompoundShellScript never tests '#'
findings.layer: shell re-parse of an appended argument list

findings.claim: All five doc surfaces state the scope limit as compound scripts only, while the code also silently skips env-prefixed scripts, nested pm delegation, and any script whose first token is neither a framework nor a known runner
findings.evidence: probe: "NODE_ENV=development vite" and "npm run dev:vite" both return with zero flags injected (findFrameworkIndex returns null; npm is not in PACKAGE_RUNNERS). Docs diff adds the identical '&&, |, ;' sentence to README, apps/docs/page.mdx, apps/docs/configuration/page.mdx, SKILL.md and cli.ts --help. The PR body itself lists four skip classes

issue_candidates.title: The Expo LAN carve-out is gated differently in its two homes
issue_candidates.evidence: cli-utils.ts uses isLanEnvEnabled() alone; cli.ts uses lanMode || isLanEnvEnabled(). A --lan flag that does not reach the helper as an env var diverges in a third way, independent of F1
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: surfaced while reading for F1; not externally reported and not part of the three findings harvested
